note: Crucible Shark Tank review findings from the Skeptic Shark.

findings.message: The plan specifies a WRITE_LOCK for atomic appends to the per-project journal but fails to address cross-process file locking and sharing on Windows when both the dashboard service and CLI tools (e.g., `anchor.py rnd events`) attempt to write to or read the journal concurrently, potentially causing sharing violations or file corruption.

The proposed 'no' branch fallback for PTYs (drain/park/warm-resume) downplays the severity of dashboard restarts. If PTYs remain dashboard-owned, restarting the dashboard will terminate the shell and any active child processes (e.g., SSH, repl, build). A 'warm-resume seed' cannot preserve running process state, resulting in complete state loss rather than a simple 'warm reconnect.'

findings.section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 — Declarative Route Table & Default-Deny Auth (C2)
findings.criterion: 2. One route table, declarative auth, default-deny.
findings.message: The plan fails to define the mechanism by which the browser obtains the auth cookie. If the GET data plane is default-deny, the browser cannot load the dashboard to prompt the user for a token unless a specific unauthenticated bootstrap/login route is explicitly designed, allowlisted, and secure against token extraction.

findings.section: Phase 1 — Phase 0 — Ground Truth & Safety Rails (pre-wave instrumentation)
findings.message: The phrasing 'runs 20× nightly' in Phase 0 and Phase 7 is ambiguous and contradicts the '20-night healthcheck soak' in the Sizing Note. It is unclear if the safety gate requires running the walks 20 times in a single night to check for flakes, or soaking them over 20 calendar nights, which would introduce a massive 3-week serialization delay for phase completion.

The plan notes that Mitigation 9 is not cited or mapped to any phase, deferring its reconciliation to Stage 2. Since this is the Master Plan where all safety rails and mitigations should be locked, leaving a mitigation unassigned creates a gap in the safety design before Stage 2 implementation planning begins.

findings.section: Phase headings (Phase 1 — Phase 0 through Phase 7 — Phase 6)
findings.message: The phase titles exhibit a numbering mismatch (e.g. 'Phase 1 — Phase 0', 'Phase 2 — Phase 1'), which makes tracking the progression of waves confusing.
